hypothesis: The unchanged bidirectional breakout-onset provider can be evaluated as a shared-account live-research mechanism on BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE while preserving one position per coin, exact venue protection, and full opportunity accounting.
decision: Keep the authorized v14 runtime and the open SOL lifecycle unchanged while they remain technically healthy. The first executable v14 entry proves that the SOL route can produce a fresh, directionally aligned 5-minute breakout intent, obtain a mainnet IOC fill, arm a reduce-only venue stop, and remain under the persisted maximum-hold controller. Preserve the entry as unresolved forward evidence: its regime and execution context are coherent, but an open trade supplies no realized profitability evidence and its marked result is provisional.
falsifier: The technical assessment is falsified by a profile or run identity mismatch, loss of the exact SOL position or stop identity, duplicate same-coin exposure, a live fault, stale intent admission, an unprotected open position, or an exit that cannot be reconciled to the entry lifecycle. The economic hypothesis remains unproven until the SOL trade and additional non-adjacent entries resolve after fees, funding, slippage, and exit latency; repeated after-cost losses, direction concentration, or profit factor at or below one would weaken it.
limitations: The SOL lifecycle is still open, so marked PnL, drawdown, funding, and path statistics are provisional and cannot be counted as a win, loss, or profit-factor observation.
One entry proves route and execution liveness but cannot estimate repeatability, directional durability, or portfolio edge.
The favorable first 5.6-second markout does not establish path quality; the later marked path was adverse at the immutable audit cutoff.
The measured entry fee and slippage do not include the eventual exit fee, exit slippage, future funding, or stop gap risk.
Setup readiness and regime confidence are prerequisite telemetry rather than calibrated win probabilities.
No strategy, position, order, sizing policy, execution scope, or running process changed as a result of this journal revision.
